newsitem.title: CANADA: Laidlaw unit sale "not dilutive" - CEO.
newsitem.headline: Laidlaw unit sale "not dilutive" - CEO.

text.p: Laidlaw Inc chief executive James Bullock said on Wednesday that the US$1.65 billion sale of its solid waste unit to Allied Waste Industries Inc would not dilute earnings.
"It's not dilutive," Bullock told Reuters in a telephone interview.

Bullock called today's deal, in the works since late spring, a "win-win situation" for both sides. Laidlaw becomes a 20 percent shareholder in Arizona-based Allied Waste, which can increase its solid waste business.

Bullock added the deal gave the waste and transportation firm a cash boost. "It provides a significant gain for Laidlaw at this stage. The assets we're selling have a book cost of just over US$800 million, so our pre-tax gain is US$800 million and our after-tax is about US$600 million."

"It's a pretty good day for Laidlaw shareholders," he said.Laidlaw Class B shares topped the most actives on the Toronto Stock Exchange, rising 1.05 to 15.35 on nearly five million shares. They passed a year high of 15.00 set in early April. Class A shares rose 1.35 to 15.50 on moderate dealings, overtaking a former record of 14.875 in April.

Laidlaw stock gained moderate ground last week after rumors swirled that Republic Industries Inc would buy the solid waste unit for about US$1 billion, and Laidlaw would use the funds to repurchase shares from major shareholder Canadian Pacific Ltd.
CP has a 47.2 percent voting interest in Laidlaw.

Bullock said Laidlaw had never spoken to Republic but did exclude buying back CP's stake. "Not ruling it out, but I'm certainly not saying by any means it's at the top of the list either. We've got lots of opportunities to grow in our other businesses."
Bullock added that "we have to reinvest the money as we see in the best interests of the shareholders."

Bullock also did not rule out buying other transportation businesses after swallowing the transportation division of Scotts Hospitality Inc earlier this year. It has the largest school transportation units in North America. "Stay tuned," Bullock said.
"We want to build on the strength of both of our ambulance and our bus group."

"Laidlaw now has a balance sheet with almost US$3 billion of shareholders equity and net debt of about US$500 million. We have capacity for opportunities that will come along for each of these three businesses (school busing, ambulances and hazardous waste)."

He joked that his first choice would be to play with the cash. "I think I'll put the money on the floor of my office and run around in it for a couple of days. We've been working night and day to get this done," Bullock said. "I think I'll get some sleep."
